title: The Buras crowd, music and Delacroix Island
summary: The down-river crowd wanted Dixieland and jazz; fishermen and trappers paid at the door; he played Delacroix Island too.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: What sort of music did they like down there? Was it regular Dixieland type or whatever you want to call it?
Dixieland and jazz, I mean.
I didn't know if a lot of the people started Cajuns or what they are down there, if they liked it.
Well, I got Free Jacks, I mean, whatever you call them.
But they played the same kind of music there?

All the time, I mean, that's what they wanted. I mean, you couldn't go down with no Chitterbug like they do now down there. They didn't go for that. You go down there and now you play that kind of music. That's right. Yeah, certain ones you had to play that.
Yeah, like that Dixieland and jazz.
And they'll ask you too, if they call you, I mean, do you play Dixieland and jazz? Some of them placed down there, you said, no, they don't want you.
No. You go down there every week then?
Every Friday, every Saturday we go down there.
Just the local people, wouldn't it be people from here sometime go down or tourists or what kind of crowd did you have?

They had their own crowd. They had their own crowd. They would come from different sections, you know, Venus. People from Burst would come to Venus, I mean, and Potash, all them different places down there. I mean, they'd come there. They know New Orleans people all there. They're selling them.
Most of the people come from, say, from where they're from, all the time, all the time, all the time. Yeah, all the time, all the time. Like that.
But are they mostly down there trappers or fisher rooms?
Fisher, trappers and...
People like that.
Food and more. Artists and that, all the things like that. Yeah. The old people that have money, I mean, they pay $2, $3 to come in the dance.
The regular dance is a charge to get in charge at the door and then to get in. That's right. I know they still have music. They have an orange festival. I've been wanting to go down every year.
They got some, I know who's going down there, but they got some bands going down there. I know who's going down there.
Andy Anderson went about a year ago, I know. He was going down there.

Andrew Anderson. I played with, I played with them. Trumpet players. I forget who else was in the band. I worked in Delacue Island too. I worked down there. But not, not, not regular. I worked down there a couple of nights, I mean.
That's on this side over the other side. Yeah, about the Salmon Hall.
Salmon Hall, Salmon Hall.
Anybody go in there? Spanish people there, or are they mostly there? French and Spanish.
French and Spanish. All mixed up there.
And you go there, do you play the same type of music?
Same type, yeah. Same type, yeah.
Same type down there.
